coco-si.meta_description: 493 expert personas across 13 departments, 231 skills, and 389 commands inside Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 13 more coding tools.
coco-si.does_for_you: Coco Super Intelligence seats an advisory board of expert personas inside the coding tool you already use. You ask one hard question, the board argues it out, you get one pick with the dissent named, and your local skills, commands and agents then do the work.
coco-si.who_detail: You already work in Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and the calls that hurt are the ones with no obvious answer: architecture, scope, risk, go or no-go. You want the strongest objections on the table before you commit.
does: 16 to 32 personas on /SI-Decide
Ask one hard question with /SI-Decide and it seats 16 to 32 of 493 personas across 13 departments; add --debate for reaction rounds before the vote.
Named dissent, not an average
Every advisory round records who disagreed and why, backed by an offline checker that enforces persona source and held-status rules.
Skills, commands and agents that do the work
Ships 231 skills, 389 commands and 41 agents; a default Claude Code install delivers 193 of the skills.
One command, 16 coding tools
One command, npx cocosuperintelligence, installs into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code and 12 other coding tools (16 adapters).
Runs on your own machine, no telemetry
Files and state stay on your machine with no telemetry; your coding tool keeps its own model provider and keys.

try.heading: Install in one step
try.lead: Run one command in a terminal. It clones the pinned v2.4.0 release tag into ./coco and wires your coding agent locally.
try.note: Open-core: the core framework is Apache-2.0 and the Super Intelligence board is proprietary. Remove it any time with --uninstall, which removes only what the install recorded and restores your original files.

voice.meta_description: Private on-device speech-to-text and cited meeting notes for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Works offline with open models. MIT licensed.
voice.os: macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows x64, Linux x64 and arm64
voice.does_for_you: Coco Voice is private speech-to-text on your own computer. Hold a key and your words are typed into the app you already have open, transcripts are tidied locally, and meetings are saved as cited notes on disk, with no account and no subscription.
voice.who_detail: You dictate emails, code comments or notes all day, or sit in meetings you later need to search, and you would rather the audio and text stayed on your own machine than went to a cloud service.

try_above.label: Download v0.20.9
try_above.note: macOS, Windows x64, and Linux x64 and arm64 installers on GitHub Releases.

does: Hold-to-talk dictation into any app
Option+Space on macOS, Ctrl+Space on Windows and Linux, or toggle mode. Recognition works offline once your speech model is downloaded.
Meeting notes with speakers and citations
Grouped Home, Meetings and Voice screens with live recording controls, a dual-track speaker view, segment citations, cross-meeting to-dos and local BM25 cited Q&A saved on disk.
Local clean-up and your own words
A local Qwen3-4B model on Mac tidies text and drops spoken self-corrections such as “scratch that”, alongside custom vocabulary and local history.
Open speech models, checked before use
Pick an open speech model, including Whisper, Parakeet and Moonshine. Each download shows its licence and is checked against a pinned SHA-256 before use.

signal.meta_description: Signal is Coco Research's open design language: three editions, Light Paper and Dark Stage CSS tokens, and rules for legible interfaces. Apache-2.0.
signal.does_for_you: Signal is Coco Research’s design language. It gives your product a coherent look without a design team: a type scale, Light Paper and Dark Stage colour tokens, and written rules for keeping an interface legible.
signal.who_detail: You are building a site or app and want a ready-made, accessible look you can read, copy and adapt, with light and dark themes that already work on desktop and phone.
does: Three editions, light and dark
Three editions with first-class Light Paper and Dark Stage tokens across desktop and phone viewports.
Readable type with steady numbers
Archivo and Martian Mono variable typography with tabular numerals for counts and baselines.
No tracking, no network calls
Static stylesheets and page scripts make zero runtime network requests, analytics beacons or tracking calls.
Respects reduced motion
Native prefers-reduced-motion rules switch transitions and WebGL motion off cleanly.
status: A browser and a text editor; static CSS and docs
Static stylesheets and scripts make no runtime network requests
next: No packaged release yet
Use the CSS and docs straight from the repository. No release is tagged and no date is announced.

mira.who_detail: You make short-form video, you are comfortable running a Python project, and you want the work done locally. The repository is archived, so it is best treated as reference you can read and fork.

heliopause.meta_description: Heliopause by Coco Research gives local AI tools a Lead and roles on your machine, serving a live status board over loopback. Apache-2.0, v0.7.3.
kns: Local live view on your machine
heliopause.does_for_you: Heliopause gives your AI tools a Lead and roles, like a small company, and shows who is working, idle, blocked or waiting on you in a live status page that runs only on your own machine.
heliopause.who_detail: You run several AI coding tools or agents at once and lose track of which one is doing what. You want one local view, with no account and no cloud.
does: A live map of your agents
Shows each agent as working, idle, blocked or needs-you, with its latest line and pulse links.
Local only, no account
A loopback-only local server with no account, no telemetry and no remote sync.
A sample company to try first
Includes a built-in sample company preview before you point it at your own folders.
No packages to install
Runs on the Python standard library and git, with zero external Python package dependencies.
SHA-256 digests and an ED25519-signed manifest
Release archives ship with SHA-256 digests and an ED25519-signed manifest you can verify with ssh-keygen.
